presidentialSuccession.name: Gustavo Petro
presidentialSuccession.notes: First left president of Colombia. FSP membership of the Pacto Histórico coalition as such is not established here (to verify): its constituent Polo Democrático Alternativo and Partido Comunista Colombiano appear in Regalado's 2007 FSP roster, and forodesaopaulo.org published a solidarity statement with Petro and the Pacto Histórico. Petro's political lineage runs through the M-19 (see Armed movements) and the Polo Democrático. His term ends on 7 August 2026: Abelardo de la Espriella (Movimiento de Salvación Nacional) defeated Iván Cepeda (Pacto Histórico) in the 21 June 2026 runoff by 0.96 points — the narrowest presidential runoff in Colombian history; the CNE certified the result on 24 June, Cepeda conceded the same day, and Petro recognized the result while alleging fraud (his characterization). The inauguration is scheduled for 7 August 2026 and had not yet occurred as of this dataset's date.

fspParties.note: Colombia's FSP members include the Partido Comunista Colombiano and the Unión Patriótica — long marginal and, in the UP's case, the target of a genocidal extermination campaign in the 1980s–90s — and today Gustavo Petro's Pacto Histórico. Colombia's left was excluded from national power for the whole armed-conflict era; Petro's 2022 win was the first by a left candidate.

legislativeControl.seats: For the entire post-1990 period Colombia's FSP-aligned left held only a small share of Congress and never the presidency; the Unión Patriótica was decimated by political violence.
Petro's Pacto Histórico became the largest bloc in both chambers in 2022 but well short of a majority; his government depends on a shifting, fragile congressional coalition.

The Congress elected in March 2026 was seated on 20 July 2026 (103 senators, 183 representatives). Pacto Histórico — the FSP member — remains the largest single Senate bloc on the CNE-certified roll (26 seats per Finance Colombia's report of Resolution 3328/2026; other published tallies differ by one seat in three rows, a discrepancy recorded rather than resolved). A complete certified Chamber table had not been obtained as of this update (to verify).
